memory_update.text: TYL should remain the public-sector vertical-software reference benchmark for this node, but it is too well-known and too large to be the main underfollowed discovery target.

APPN is a plausible underfollowed government-modernization workflow candidate because its public-sector use cases include procurement, grants, case management, ERP modernization, and defense workflows; verify government revenue share and recurring mix.

CLBT is a stronger underfollowed candidate than generic government IT services because public-sector customers accounted for more than 90% of its 2024 revenue and its digital-investigation workflow is compliance-heavy.

SSTI is a below-USD-300M speculative exception: highly node-relevant public-safety workflow exposure, but political controversy, municipal contract risk, and product concentration must be treated as primary falsification factors.

Need a follow-up pass for grant-management, permitting, courts, welfare/benefits administration, procurement analytics, and education-administration vendors that may be private, acquired, or buried inside larger US-listed distributors/integrators.

node: Government modernization, compliance, and regulated-workflow software
summary: Layer 1B expanded the universe around public-sector modernization software with a two-lane funnel. Tyler Technologies is retained as the pure-play reference anchor, while Appian, Cellebrite, and SoundThinking form the underfollowed discovery lane. The strongest underfollowed fits are vendors whose products sit inside agency workflows that regulation and government-spending complexity can make stickier: procurement, grants, case management, digital investigations, public safety analytics, FedRAMP/cloud authorization, and compliance-heavy agency operations. This is research support only, not a trading recommendation.
